rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_supervised-claude-agentic: proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, proj_kernel=3, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=5, img_sx=0.5, img_sy=0.5, img_sr=0.02, lr=0.005, epochs=8, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 feasibility (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). dual_domain_bilateral_supervised = the SUPERVISED dual-domain stack with the image-domain U-Net SWAPPED for a trainable BILATERAL FILTER (Wagner 2022): proj_dn(BF stack) -> FBP(full 2304 views) -> img_dn(BF stack), MSE-vs-truth + lambda_neg negativity penalty. NOT the per-image N2I bilateral variant. SHARES the sibling dual_domain_supervised Mayo path exactly: staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps (mayo_per_sample_setup/_fbp, per-sample pipe.R_full swap), bg_target=truth, val=ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override). GOAL: does the bilateral variant RUN on Mayo under the corrected path and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png within the HARD 20-min train+score budget, establishing where the bilateral-supervised baseline lands vs the dual_domain_supervised U-Net (which scored SSIM 0.8880 / hr 0.2759 at c=16/lr=1e-4/ep=8 on the SAME 214-slice 321px-FOV metric, search-20260619-01 iter-1). CONFIG: started from that sibling iter-1 cfg and changed ONLY the image module (U-Net -> bilateral). proj_dn = 1 BF (kernel 3, sx=0.01 along-detector tiny to avoid radial blur, sy=0.3 along-angle, sr=0.0005), img_dn = 3 chained BFs (kernel 5, sx=sy=0.5, sr=0.02) = a SANE MID bilateral depth/kernel (solver default is img_n_bf=1; the discarded boundary-slice TPE hinted img_n_bf=7 which is heavy/over-parameterised for a baseline -- mid=3 establishes the corrected-metric baseline, defer depth as the iter-2 knob). ~24 trainable params total (3 per BF). lr=5e-3 = Wagner BF lr (BF learns scalar sigmas; the U-Net 1e-4 would barely move them in 8 epochs), grad_clip=1.0 kept as a safety on the 2304-view FBP adjoint (the tiny BF params are far less prone to the gradient explosion that forced lr=1e-4 on the U-Net). epochs=8, lambda_neg=1.0, train_n=200 (loader rotates the 4 Wagner train patients ps-pool -> ~400 effective slices/epoch), val_n=214 = ALL L277 slices, batch_size=1 + val_chunk=1 FORCED by per-sample-ps. SIZING: the sibling U-Net (0.47M params) ran 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 419s (~7 min); the BF has ~24 params and per-step cost is dominated by the SHARED FBP adjoint (identical to the U-Net path), not the filter, so this run is comparable-or-cheaper -> comfortably inside the 20-min budget (30-min sbatch wall). HYPOTHESIS: the bilateral-supervised variant trains stably (no NaN, grad-clip holds) and produces a finite val_ssim, but UNDER-PERFORMS the dual_domain_supervised U-Net (SSIM 0.8880 / hr 0.2759) -- expect LOWER hr than 0.2759 -- because the BF has ~24 params vs the U-Net 0.47M, far less capacity to denoise the 2304-view Mayo FBP; the value here is interpretability/few-params, not peak SSIM. This onboarding iter establishes WHERE the bilateral baseline lands under the corrected 214-slice 321px-FOV metric; iter-2+ tunes ONE knob (img_n_bf depth first, then the Mayo-specific proj_sr over-smoothing lever).
